title: AgentTailor: A Semantic-Aware LLM-Based Multi-Agent System with Actor-Critic Structure
one_liner: Cut wasted agent-to-agent chatter by estimating which communication links add decision value and pruning the links that do not.
lead: Multi-agent systems often spend a large share of their budget on agents talking to one another. More communication can help only when a message changes the final decision because a repeated or irrelevant message adds cost without adding new evidence. AgentTailor asks a sharper question than most earlier work: which communication edges are actually useful? It scores edges by their semantic contribution, then trains a lightweight predictor to estimate that usefulness through virtual execution before paying for the full model calls. The result is a communication structure that keeps the helpful links and drops the redundant ones.

problem.h2: Why more agent communication is not always better
paras: In a multi-agent system, one agent often sends its intermediate conclusion to several others. That can be useful when the message changes how the receiver reasons. It is wasteful when the receiver already had the same evidence or when the message adds detail that never affects the final answer.

Many systems optimize communication only at the structural level: who is connected to whom. But that misses the real issue. Two edges with the same shape can have very different value depending on what they transmit. AgentTailor focuses on semantic contribution, meaning whether a specific communication edge actually improves the final decision because it carries evidence that the receiver did not already have and that evidence changes the receiver's choice.

callout.html: A communication edge should survive only when the message it carries changes the final decision enough to justify its cost.

steps.text: Agents exchange messages while trying to solve a shared decision problem.
Estimate how much each communication edge changes the final decision quality.
Use a lightweight network to forecast edge usefulness through virtual execution without paying for every full model call.
Drop or suppress edges whose expected contribution is small.
Solve the task with a communication pattern that preserves the helpful links and removes redundant ones.

paras: The paper changes the communication graph during execution. Instead of using a fixed set of message links, it keeps a tailored subset chosen by estimated semantic contribution.
object.object: the active communication edges between agents

hidden.name: edge utility
paras: The key hidden quantity is the value of one communication edge. An edge has high utility when the message changes a receiver's reasoning enough to improve the final answer because it introduces evidence or correction that alters the receiver's choice. It has low utility when the message is redundant, stale, or irrelevant.

AgentTailor makes this quantity operational. It tries to predict edge utility before paying to send the full message. That matters because cost falls only when the system can identify wasted edges ahead of time, not after the budget is already spent.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark edges whose messages materially change the final decision.

reads.html: The method wants to know which conversations actually matter before paying for them.
Communication should be optimized by semantic contribution rather than graph shape alone, because only some edges improve the final decision enough to justify their cost.

mechanism.h2: Why edge prediction saves budget without collapsing quality
paras: The method separates message value estimation from full message generation. Full multi-agent communication is expensive because each live edge can trigger another model call and another growing context. If the system can cheaply estimate that an edge is unlikely to help, it can suppress that edge before spending the budget because the edge would add cost without adding enough new evidence to change the answer.

The edge prediction network is useful for exactly that reason. It performs a lightweight virtual execution step that estimates whether the message along an edge is likely to improve the final decision. Helpful edges are kept because they are expected to influence the answer. Weak edges are dropped because they mostly repeat what other agents already know. The paper's reported savings make sense because the system removes low-value exchanges rather than just shrinking every message uniformly.

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose edge A->B has predicted utility 0.72 and edge C->B has predicted utility 0.18.
The second edge is dropped because its expected decision gain is too small to justify another message.

math.note: The paper's implementation is richer, but the core decision is this: keep an edge only when its expected contribution clears a cost-aware threshold.

charts.title: Dense unfiltered communication
charts.note: A dense graph can work, but much of the cost is spent on exchanges that do not change the outcome.

charts.title: AgentTailor
charts.note: Accuracy improves while cost falls because the system keeps the edges that carry distinctive evidence and removes the ones that mostly echo others.

items.b: A useful edge can be pruned by mistake.
items.html: If the predictor underrates an edge that carries rare but important evidence, the final decision can suffer because that evidence never reaches the right agent.

items.b: Utility can change during the task.
items.html: An edge that was weak early can become valuable later, because new evidence changes what other agents still need to hear.

items.b: Virtual execution can be too coarse.
items.html: If the lightweight predictor does not approximate real interaction closely enough, it may keep cheap but unhelpful edges or drop expensive but necessary ones.
The system should re-estimate edge value as the task evolves so the communication graph follows the information needs of the agents rather than staying frozen.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a four-agent system for a classification or reasoning task where each agent sees a different slice of evidence. Run one version with all communication edges active and a second version with an edge predictor that can suppress low-value links before messages are sent.

Measure final accuracy, number of active edges, and total message cost. The demo should show that the tailored graph keeps accuracy high because it preserves the few edges that actually change the final answer while removing many exchanges that do not.
demo.closing: If efficiency rises after pruning, the system is learning which conversations are worth paying for.
